correctness.rationale: For all m,n >= 2, the closed-neighborhood condition is equivalent to x_ij=1+r_i+c_j. The consistency equations (n+1)r_i=n+T and (m+1)c_j=m+T give a complete four-parity classification. Uniqueness of odd--odd row/column parameters follows from their being actual parities. Counting gives all coefficients. The affine-in-a optimization proves every minimum and all minimizers. Independent exhaustive neighborhood enumeration for 2<=m,n<=4 and direct GF(2) Gaussian affine enumeration for 2<=m,n<=7 reproduce full histograms. Both scripts run successfully as standalone files. The all-size proof is symbolic, not experimental.

value.rationale: A full size enumerator of all legal binary Lights Out press sets answers a mathematically natural question not resolved by the count or nullity of the solution affine space: how many solutions exist at each number of presses, and what all optimal patterns look like. The rectangular rook graph is a canonical graph family. Its four parity regimes and unique diagonal-rectangle geometry give an all-parameter structural theorem, with sharp minimum counts and a strong even-even versus odd-side phase transition. This is neither a small finite census nor a mere restatement of the known nullity.
